Translation goal: reverse-translatability for the Tafsir reader — readers should be able to map English back to JA. Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: Then God spoke to Moses in speech.
translations.2: Command the sons of Israel that they bring you pure olive oil, pressed for giving light, to kindle the lamp with it continually.
translations.3: Outside the veil of the testimony, in the tent of the presence, Aaron shall arrange it from evening until morning before God continually — an ordinance forever.
translations.4: Upon the pure lampstand shall he set them in order before God continually.
translations.5: And take fine flour, and bake it into twelve loaves, and let each loaf be of twenty [parts].
translations.6: And set them in two rows, six in each row, upon the pure table before God.
translations.7: And place upon each row pure frankincense, and let it serve as the fragrant portion from the bread — an offering to God.
translations.8: And on every Sabbath day he shall arrange them before God continually, from the sons of Israel — a covenant forever.
translations.9: Then it shall be given over to Aaron and his sons; they shall eat it in a consecrated place, for it belongs to them from the choicest of the sacred things, from the offerings to God — an ordinance forever.
translations.10: And there went out the son of an Israelite woman — he being the son of an Egyptian man — among the sons of Israel; and they quarreled in the camp, this son of the Israelite woman and the Israelite man.
translations.11: And the son of the Israelite woman reviled the Name and cursed it; and they brought him to Moses. Now the name of his mother was Shelomith daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
translations.12: And they placed him in custody, until his case should be made clear to them by the word of God.
translations.13: Then God spoke to Moses in speech.
translations.14: "Bring out the reviler to outside the camp, and let all who heard him lay their hands upon his head; and let all the people of the presence stone him with stones."
translations.15: "And command the sons of Israel, and say to them: any person who curses his Lord shall bear his guilt."
translations.16: "And whoever reviles Him thus shall be put to death — all the people of the presence shall stone him with stones. The sojourner and the native-born are equal: whichever of them curses the Name shall be put to death."
translations.17: "And any person who kills one of the souls of the people shall be put to death."
translations.18: "And whoever kills a beast shall render its like — head in place of head."
translations.19: "And any person who inflicts a defect upon one of his fellow countrymen — as he has done, so shall be done to him."
translations.20: "Fracture in place of fracture, and eye in place of eye, and tooth in place of tooth: as one inflicts a defect upon a person, so shall it be inflicted upon him."
translations.21: "And whoever strikes a beast shall be fined; and whoever strikes a person and causes death shall be put to death."
translations.22: "And there shall be one ruling for you, in which the sojourner and the native-born are equal — for I am God, your Lord, the One."
translations.23: And Moses spoke thereby to the sons of Israel; and they brought out the reviler to outside the camp, and stoned him with stones until he died. And the sons of Israel acted in all the rest of what had come down to them, as God had commanded Moses.
